trust_decision.summary: The compiler decides whether a ternary arm's memory can be read directly with the result type's layout (no conversion) when the arm type is narrower but compatible; at the pinned commit both codegens pass the arm through unconverted, so element strides/offsets of the wider result type are applied to narrower data.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'ternary nested array selection'; parse_IfExp in the legacy (default) codegen is the obvious ternary lowering an engineer greps first.

fix_sites.entry_point: vyper compile (default legacy codegen) via compile_code -> Expr.parse_IfExp; new punnable() helper and typed create_memory_copy
vyper compile, legacy codegen: ternary expression in any statement (assign, return, log arg)
vyper compile --experimental-codegen: ternary expression with non-word, non-frame result type
vyper compile --experimental-codegen: ternary whose result is a tuple containing an INF member (dynamic tuple frame), via dynamic_tuple_frame_from_value
fix_sites.module_kind: lower-level Venom codegen context (frame/memory layout helpers)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: vyper/codegen_venom/expr.py:920-929 and vyper/codegen_venom/context.py:276-316 (Venom codegen, incl. dynamic-tuple-frame passthrough at context.py:282-283)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Venom is opt-in '--experimental-codegen' and the INF-member tuple frame path only exists there, so a solver can argue the experimental backend and Venom-only INF tuples are outside the advisory's (legacy) scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Same-layout arms (and top-level-only width differences, e.g. DynArray[uint256,2] vs DynArray[uint256,5], Bytes[10] vs Bytes[20]) must stay zero-copy/pointer passthrough; the fix's own test asserts arms remain literal variables in legacy IR and no typed_dyn_copy in Venom. An over-broad 'always copy arms' fix breaks that and storage/calldata-located arms' location handling.

tuple with narrower bytestring member (from internal call or local)

O7_producer.where: vyper/codegen_venom/context.py:276-316 (dynamic_tuple_frame_from_value: maps tuple values into the Venom-only frame layout; early-returns frame-typed values unchanged at :282-283)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Venom memory store of a narrower tuple into a wider tuple type (tuple local assignment / internal memory return) falls to a raw same-size copy because TupleT equality compares only the empty 'members' dict, so 'src_typ != typ' is always False for tuples.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Not a ternary; the advisory is about ternary selection, and the fix's own comment (fix.diff:567-568) acknowledges the TupleT.__eq__ quirk but works around it only for ternaries, so a solver can call it a separate pre-existing bug.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: vyper/semantics/types/subscriptable.py:399 + vyper/semantics/types/base.py:128-133 (cause) reached from vyper/codegen_venom/stmt.py:280 and vyper/codegen_venom/stmt.py:1182; 3 files, 2 packages from landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: list literal [a, b] whose elements have narrower element layouts than the list's value type, emitted as a bare 'multi' without per-element conversion
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: parse_List already passes element IR through as-is and relies on make_setter downstream; a maintainer could add a fast-path that copies the multi as a block.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: tuple literal frame path storing a member pointer without layout conversion when member type is a narrower bounded sequence
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same frame construction pattern as the fixed dynamic_tuple_frame_from_value; skipping materialize for 'already memory' members is a natural optimisation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: dynamic tuple internal return normalisation guarded by '!=' on member types (would silently skip if a member were itself a tuple/struct-equality-quirk type)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Uses the same '!=' layout test whose TupleT semantics are broken.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap both arms in legacy parse_IfExp with ensure_in_memory/make_setter to the result type (always copy), leaving Venom and the INF tuple frame path untouched.
